This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Triplet chords (12/8)**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

The chord on all three eighth notes of every beat, the doo-wop piano part. In 4/4 they are played as triplets.

It belongs in *12/8 doo-wop*. Here it is in the 12/8 doo-wop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Triplet chords (12/8)","opts":{"compRhythm":"triplets"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-quarters.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Triplet chords (12/8), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The chord on all three eighths of every beat: 1-and-a, 2-and-a. Right hand, light repeated chords from the wrist; left hand, the root on 1 and 3. Lean slightly on each beat.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Triplet chords (12/8)","opts":{"compRhythm":"triplets"}},{"label":"Quarter-note chords (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 66 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Triplet chords (12/8)","opts":{"compRhythm":"triplets"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C Am|F G|C Am|F G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Triplet chords (12/8)","opts":{"compRhythm":"triplets"}}]'></div>
